title: biset.md/MessengerCapability
description: Biset's own capability credential type, presented by a did:webvh wallet (dito or any other implementation) as a VC-DM 2.0 Verifiable Credential (see ~/did.md/PLAN3-oid4vp-transport.md -- the transport envelope moved from a flat {document,proof} pair to this VC-DM wrapping). Biset owns the credentialSubject content, not did.md -- did.md's OAuth server only checks the generic transport envelope (@context/id/type/issuer/credentialSubject/proof, and within credentialSubject: audience/expiresAt/issuedAt/scope, deviceJkt/authorizationDetails present-or-absent) and a Data Integrity Proof over the whole credential; it does not interpret credentialSubject's contents. This file is imported directly by did-md-oauth.ts (see json-schema.ts) and is the single source of truth for the credential SHAPE -- checks that depend on the pending authorization request (audience match, deviceJkt match, expiry-in-the-past, required scope membership) are NOT expressible here and remain in did-md-oauth.ts itself. See ~/did.md/PLAN2-capability-ownership.md and ~/did.md/SPEC.md §5.3 for the design rationale.

id.description: A fresh urn:uuid per authorization; not reused across grants.

prefixItems.description: "biset.md/MessengerCapability" is Biset's own name and the only value Biset's own requests ask for (capability_type on the /authorize request). "did.md/DeviceCapability" is accepted here too, for a did.md Wallet that predates the capability_type request parameter and so falls back to its own old default -- a transitional compatibility value, not a name Biset chose.

issuer.description: The subject's own did:webvh -- the DID whose authentication key signed this credential's Data Integrity Proof.

audience.description: did.md's OAuth client_id for this Biset registration: either an RFC 7591 Dynamic Client Registration id, or (PLAN6) the did:webvh DID Biset authenticated itself with via JAR when running at https://t.biset.md.

deviceJkt.description: RFC 9449 DPoP JWK SHA-256 thumbprint of Biset's device key. Always present: Biset always requests dpop_jkt (see redirectToWallet), so a Biset capability credential is always DPoP-bound.

scope.description: Biset-defined scope strings. Known values in current use: openid, profile, biset:login, biset:device, biset:routing, biset:messaging, biset:vault (see REQUESTED_SCOPES in did-md-oauth.ts). did.md's server checks these only against the client's OWN registered scope list -- it does not know what any of them mean.

authorizationDetails.description: RFC 9396 Rich Authorization Details, opaque to did.md's server. Biset requests a fixed set of detail types per authorization (see redirectToWallet in did-md-oauth.ts) and validates each echoed detail itself (capabilityDetails).

proof.description: A W3C Data Integrity Proof over this credential (with `proof` itself excluded from what is hashed -- see verifyProof in did-md-oauth.ts, and verifyAuthenticationProof in did.md's server.ts). Only the shape did-md-oauth.ts's own checks need is required here; the actual cryptographic verification is not a JSON Schema concern.

didDocumentEditDetail.description: Present only when Biset's authorization request included urn:did-core:document-edit:v1 (device onboarding that adds a verificationMethod to the identity's DID Document). See didDocumentEditDetail in did-md-oauth.ts for the exact validation this echoes against.
